system.summary: System Y: a simple substitution with codes of one or two digits and no homophones. Even digits alone are vowels (0 i, 2 o, 4 e, 6 a); odd digits alone are m n s r (1 3 5 7); two-digit codes give the other consonants and u (13 z, 15 t, 17 l, 19 q, 29 p, 39 h, 49 g, 51 u, 59 f, 69 d, 79 c, 89 b); 8 and 9 alone, and 31, are nulls. No word division; the text is parsed longest code first. The same system as Camillo Capilupi's letters c. 48 and c. 49r in capilupi1545. System X (03r, 09r) is a different hand and system, not attacked.

prior_solution.where: Nothing in the repository, the issues or catalogue 1555. The capilupi1545 notes (WAINUT) list the images of Ippolito cc. 80a-80h among items compared and rejected as keys for Camillo's 1545 letter; they were not deciphered there. No printed edition was checked.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout directed the work, approved sending the problem to Claude Fable 5.2 after the Opus attempts failed, and decided what to publish. Claude Opus 5.5 agents transcribed and arbitrated the images, wrote and froze the protocol, made the failed key attempts, froze the proposed key, ran the gate and the single measure. Claude Fable 5.2 (API) proposed the key. Claude Opus 5.5 (API) made the word count and the reading. No human palaeographer checked the transcription or the reading.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription and arbitration, protocol, failed key attempts, freezing of the key, gate, measure)
Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), via the API (key proposal and first decoding of the training folios)
Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via the API (word count by the README rule, reading and review)

solution.what: Nine images transcribed in two blind passes by 12 Claude Opus 5.5 agents using different cropping methods. The first passes merged the short 7 (= 7) and the long descending hook (= 9) of the cursive hand and were redone. Agreement between passes 98.5-99.8 % per Y folio, 93.5 % on 03r, 85 % on 09r; 150 differences arbitrated on the image (ARBITRATION.tsv); frozen 20:07 CET (SHA256-FINAL.txt).

Two hands and systems: X (03r, 09r: overlined 9, separators, clear text and partial glosses) and Y (the other folios, cursive). Y has the same absent digit pairs (09, 99, 53; 73 nearly absent) and the same recurring units (9170, 1951+even, 7939+even) as Camillo Capilupi's c. 48 and c. 49r in capilupi1545: same system. The glosses of X are partial and not alignable: no crib.

PREREG-1555.md frozen 19:35 CET (SHA-256 b7c34cfe...8c49; measure_1555.py b65938e6...c49c) before any key-building: held-out portion H = all of 05r; single measure M = share of decoded letters covered by Italian words of 3 letters or more; 200 controls permuting the plaintext values; PASS iff M > max(controls) and M >= 0.60; one run only, behind a readability gate on the training folios. Before the freeze only structural counts and one vowel-skeleton test (06r+06v) had been made; 05r had not been used.

Claude Opus 5.5, build set = Y without 05r, Camillo Capilupi cc. 44r-44v (a working dossier of ours, not submitted) and the capilupi1545 transcriptions of c. 48 and c. 49r (5,110 digits, 2,209 units odd*+even). Homophonic anneal with unit = letter: -2.46 to -2.69 per letter, restarts diverge. Syllabic C*V model: degenerate, or -2.44 to -2.55 with four different vowel tables. Nothing frozen (OPUS-ESSAI.md).

Package sent to Claude Fable 5.2 via the API at 20:16 CET: the Y and X transcriptions without 05r, the capilupi1545 c. 48 and c. 49r transcriptions, OPUS-ESSAI.md and its scripts, an Italian corpus and lexicon (leak check: 0 leaks of 05r, positive control). It proposed a simple substitution with 1-2 digit codes and no homophones, 8 and 9 alone as nulls. Frozen unchanged as KEY-1555.json at 20:56:15 CET (SHA-256 76ab7684...955e).

Gate (GATE-1555.md, 20:57 CET): our measure script decodes training folio 04r into continuous Italian ('Salviati mi ha detto che sua nipote moglie del conte di Santa Fiore...'); Fable's decoding of 02r and 06r reads the same. M on 04r 0.832 against controls max 0.162 (a check, not the measure). Gate: readable.
The single preregistered run on held-out 05r (20:58 CET): M = 0.7962; 200 controls max 0.175, mean 0.018; PASS (MESURE-1555-H.txt, verbatim).

Words counted by the README rule (sure / probable / restored / unresolved) by Claude Opus 5.5 via the API: 692 words, 631 sure, 37 probable, 20 restored, 4 unresolved; 96.5 % sure+probable, strict 91.2 %. Per folio: 02r 96.9, 04r 99.2, 05r 93.9, 05v 100 (10 words), 06r 97.2, 06v 95.1, 07r 97.6. 05r+05v together 94.3 %: read in part. A recurring 'mm' where t or l is needed (five occurrences) points to code 11 or its transcription.

Integration check: strict recount from dudout/reading.md (sure only). 631 of 692 = 91.2 % overall; by document 02r 118/128 = 92.2 %, 04r 114/118 = 96.6 %, 05r-05v 138/158 = 87.3 %, 06r-07r 261/288 = 90.6 %. Only 04r passes the 95 % bar. The contributor's sure + probable figure (96.5 %) is kept once, labelled as theirs.

Integration check: own decoder written from dudout/key.txt (23 simple codes, longest code first, no composite entries) decodes the arbitrated transcriptions to the same Italian (letter-sequence similarity to decryption.txt 0.93-0.98 per folio; differences are the parse of ambiguous strings that the unpublished ~2,000 composite entries fix). Own coverage measure on held-out 05r with a lexicon of Italian 16th-century words of frequency >= 30 (length >= 3): M = 0.83 against 200 permuted-value controls max 0.34, mean 0.16. KEY-1555.json and the contributor's lexicon are not in the repository, so M = 0.7962 and the frozen hashes could not be reproduced exactly at this point (settled by the PR #521 check below).

Integration check, image: Estense IIIF manifest of cc. 80a-80h fetched (18 images, labelled 0080-01r ... 0080-09v; the contributor's label 05r is canvas 9 = 0080-05r, penciled 80d). Lines 1-4 and the end of line 7 of 05r compared with the transcription (about 150 groups by count and shape): they agree; the 7 / 9 (short bar / hook) calls were not judged independently. At 'imperammor' (05r line 7) the image does show two short 1-shaped strokes before the 2, so the 'mm' is in the transcription as written, not a transcription slip.

Integration check, sibling test (not a claim): the simple key.txt applied to the first-pass digits of capilupi1545 c. 48 and c. 49r (Camillo Capilupi, Feb 1546) gives Italian runs ('mi ha deto hor basta trata', 'lambasciador di Francia ha deto a Ferar', 'tre di sono', 'il tene da due hore ragionando', 'suo figliuolo piglila figlia de ... re', 'lo scriuessa al re ... conditioni'), with gaps where the first-pass digits are doubtful. Those two pages were part of the build set, so this is not an independent test and no reading of them is claimed. It shows that the digit system of c. 48 and c. 49r is the same as system Y.

Second integration check (PR #521, which adds KEY-1555.json, lexicon_1555.txt and HASHES-1555.md): SHA-256 of KEY-1555.json = 76ab7684...955e and of lexicon_1555.txt = 328049d3...d533, as stated in HASHES-1555.md (the PR text's e59da4f9... is the hash of the uncommitted source corpus). The lexicon yields 6,463 words after the script's filter, as stated. measure_1555.py re-run with python3 -I on transcription_05r.txt: M 0.7962, controls max 0.175 mean 0.0181, PASS, byte-identical to MESURE-1555-H.txt. Own longest-code-first decoder from KEY-1555.json reproduces decryption.txt exactly on all seven Y folios (0 differing characters); the 1-2 digit entries equal key.txt. Freeze order and corpus-to-lexicon derivation remain by the contributor's record (no external timestamp; corpus not committed).

validation.notes: Contributor's own protocol (PREREG-1555.md, frozen before any key-building), not docs/_validate.py. One run of measure_1555.py on the held-out folio 05r: M 0.7962 against 200 permuted controls (max 0.175). The measure is lexical coverage; it validates the key as a system, not each word. The reading of 05r itself stays under the 95 % bar. Re-run at integration on 13 Nov 2026 after PR #521 added the frozen key and the lexicon: hashes match, M 0.7962 and controls max 0.175 reproduced exactly; the freeze order is by the contributor's record.

outcome.method_basis: The key of system Y was proposed by Claude Fable 5.2 from the ciphertext alone (no crib, no period table), frozen, gated on the training folios and passed one preregistered measure on the held-out folio 05r. It is partial for the target: code 11 is doubtful, and system X (03r, 09r) has no key.

outcome.notes: Two letters of Ippolito Capilupi in two cipher systems. System Y (02r, 04r, 05r, 05v, 06r, 06v, 07r) read with a key proposed by Claude Fable 5.2 and measured on the held-out folio 05r. 668 of 692 words sure or probable (96.5 %), strict 91.2 %; 05r+05v 94.3 %, read in part. System X (03r, 09r, about 1,400 of 5,773 transcribed digits) not attacked. Same system as Camillo Capilupi's c. 48 and c. 49r (capilupi1545); not the homophonic alphabet of Camillo's 8 May 1545 letter there.
outcome.fraction_read_source: dudout/reading.md, by words, system Y folios only: 692 words, 631 sure = 91.2 % (strict, README rule: probable, restored and unresolved words are holes). The contributor's own figure counts the 37 probable words as read: 668/692 = 96.5 %. System X (03r, 09r) not attacked and not counted.

texts.label: Ippolito Capilupi, Civitavecchia, 17 May, to Ferrante Gonzaga (image 02r)
texts.summary: The Count of Reggio's letter is in Salviati's hands. Salviati let Capilupi read it but refused a copy, and begs Ferrante never to show he knows of it. Capilupi learned the short letter by heart at one reading and sends it from memory, sure of the sense.

texts.label: Ippolito Capilupi, Rome, 10 May, to Ferrante Gonzaga (image 04r)
texts.summary: Salviati reports that his niece, wife of the Count of Santa Fiora, offers to arrange a marriage of Donna Ippolita to the lord of Piombino; he favours it as preserving that state. Capilupi committed to nothing and asks what to answer if pressed.

reading_review.note: read as sentences by Claude Opus 5.5 (API), 12 Nov 2026; no human review Integration check 13 Nov 2026: strict share (sure only) 114/118 = 96.6 %; the contributor's sure + probable figure was 99.2 %.

texts.label: Ippolito Capilupi, Rome, 10 May, to Ferrante Gonzaga (images 05r-05v; 05r is the held-out folio)
texts.summary: Juan de Vega still thinks Ferrante should not come to Rome: the Pope would use the visit with the French, and a rumour might spread that the Emperor means to give Siena, as at Juan de Luna's visit. If Ferrante comes on his own business the Emperor will not rebuke him but would rather he stayed away.

reading_review.note: read as sentences by Claude Opus 5.5 (API), 12 Nov 2026; no human review. 05r alone 93.9 %, with 05v 94.3 %: under the 95 % bar, read in part Integration check 13 Nov 2026: strict share (sure only) 138/158 = 87.3 %; the contributor's sure + probable figure was 94.3 %.

texts.label: Ippolito Capilupi, Rome, 10 May, to Ferrante Gonzaga (images 06r, 06v, 07r)
texts.summary: Girolamo da Correggio reports that Cardinal Farnese will serve 'our cardinal' but not Ferrante, for the Sicilian grain dispute, Monreale and the Milan negotiation. Camillo Colonna reports Farnese telling Vittoria that the Pope now consents to her marriage with Orleans. Juan de Vega says the Emperor keeps the Pope guessing, so the Pope wants Farnese sent to him.

reading_review.note: read as sentences by Claude Opus 5.5 (API), 12 Nov 2026; no human review Integration check 13 Nov 2026: strict share (sure only) 261/288 = 90.6 %; the contributor's sure + probable figure was 96.5 %.
